papers_read.title_as_printed: A machine learning-based discriminative framework for mild cognitive impairment risk in middle-aged and elderly Chinese patients with depression: evidence from CHARLS and CLHLS (Yao et al., Journal of Affective Disorders 2026)
A prediction model for the risk of developing mild cognitive impairment in older adults with sarcopenia: evidence from the CHARLS (Liu et al., Aging Clinical and Experimental Research 2025)

what_each_reports.P-27: Cross-sectional discrimination of prevalent MCI (AACD: at least 1 SD below the age-band mean) among adults 60 and over with depression (CESD-10 >= 10), CHARLS 2018 wave, n=1964. The predictors are sociodemographic and health variables (education, household registration, loneliness, IADL, dyslipidaemia, diabetes, hypertension, exercise). RF AUC 0.826 in training, 0.801 (95% CI 0.760-0.841) internal validation, 5-fold CV mean 0.791 (0.771-0.810), and external CLHLS 0.653 (0.636-0.670).
what_each_reports.P-166: Prediction of incident MCI over the next four years (AACD plus no IADL disability) among cognitively normal older adults with sarcopenia, CHARLS 2011-2015 (n=414), from 8 anthropometric/functional variables (ASM, SMI, BMI, grip, walk time, depression, SPPB, sleep) with a feed-forward neural network. Test AUC 0.708 (0.544-0.844); temporal validation on CHARLS 2015-2018 (n=156) AUC 0.711 (0.588-0.823).

quantity_a: AUC for prevalent (cross-sectional) MCI among depressed adults 60 and over, CHARLS 2018, sociodemographic/health predictors
quantity_b: AUC for 4-year incident MCI among cognitively normal sarcopenic adults, CHARLS 2011-2018, anthropometric/physical-function predictors
incompatible_if_same: No. Even as one quantity the intervals overlap: P-27's internal validation AUC 0.801 (0.760-0.841) against P-166's 0.708 (0.544-0.844) test and 0.711 (0.588-0.823) validation. P-27's own external AUC is 0.653, below P-166's.

gates.task: mismatch: cross-sectional MCI discrimination (P-27 authors call it 'discriminative', not predictive) vs 4-year incident MCI prediction
gates.dataset_family: match: both CHARLS. The waves differ (2018 vs 2011-2015/2015-2018), and overlapping respondents are possible, which is recorded as non-independence.
gates.validation_tier: mismatch: P-27 has an external CLHLS cohort (V4); P-166 has only internal test plus a temporal CHARLS split (V3). The record's 0.826 is P-27's training AUC.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible endpoint: prevalent MCI (AACD on the 31-point CHARLS battery, depressed population) vs incident MCI within 4 years (AACD on a 21-point battery plus no IADL disability, sarcopenic, cognitively normal at baseline). The metric (AUC) matches.
performance_validity: flag does not apply (no AUC at or above 0.97)
independence: Shared cohort family (CHARLS), so participants may overlap across waves. Different authors (Chengdu vs Nanjing).
grounds: The endpoint differs: P-27 discriminates prevalent MCI cross-sectionally in 2018, while P-166 predicts MCI incidence over the next four years in people cognitively normal at baseline.

The population behind the label differs (depressed adults vs sarcopenic adults), and so do the predictor sets (sociodemographic/psychosocial vs anthropometric/physical function) and the MCI definition (P-166 adds no IADL disability).
The task and validation-tier gates fail with no waiver, and the reported intervals overlap in any case.

evidence_quotes.quote: In internal testing, the random forest (RF) achieved the best predictive performance (AUC = 0.826 in training and 0.801 in internal validation)
In the validation set, RF (0.801, 95 % CI: 0.760–0.841) showed a higher AUC value compared to other ML models
Using the cohort from CLHLS for external validation, the AUC (0.653, 95 % CI: 0.636–0.670) of RF did not reach the level of the validation set
we limited the analysis to the dataset of 2018 instead of conducting a longitudinal analysis
Our model forecasts MCI incidence over the next four years, categorizing patients into low and high-risk groups based on their risk levels.
Independent validation using 2015–2018 CHARLS data confirmed the model’s efficacy, with an AUC of 0.711 (0.95 CI, 0.588–0.823).
Only longitudinal data with normal cognitive function at baseline measurement and with indicators of cognitive and activities of daily living (ADL) outcomes were included.

record_defects: claim_a 'P-27: AUC 0.826' is the training-set AUC. The internal-validation AUC is 0.801 (the registry Best_Metric) and the external one is 0.653.

claim_a/claim_b 'on T1': P-166 is incident-MCI prediction, and P-27 is cross-sectional discrimination of prevalent MCI in a depressed population. Neither is a general MCI-vs-control detection task, and the two differ from each other.
task_equal 'Yes' and validation_comparable 'Yes' are wrong: prevalent vs incident endpoint; V4 vs V3.
resolution_note 'Same architecture family (A1_classical)' is wrong for P-166, whose model is a 4-layer feed-forward neural network (logistic regression only as comparator).
The bridging evidence (P-25 AUC 0.77, P-323 AUC 0.80) is generic and identifies no separating condition, so the partially_resolved status is not supported.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Only if both studies estimated the same endpoint (same horizon, same MCI definition) in the same population with the same predictors and non-overlapping uncertainty. They do not.
